slides.title: 5 winter driving myths that could land you in a ditch

slides.myth: All-wheel drive helps you stop on ice and snow.
slides.fact: AWD and 4WD help you get moving. They don't help you brake or turn. That's all tire grip, which is why winter tires matter more.

slides.myth: Let some air out of your tires for better grip in snow.
slides.fact: Tire makers say never do this. It doesn't add traction on snow or ice, and driving on underinflated tires can damage them.

slides.myth: Hot water is a quick, safe way to clear an icy windshield.
slides.fact: The sudden heat makes the glass expand fast, and that can crack it. Use your defroster and let the glass warm up gradually.

slides.myth: Pump the brakes on ice, even if your car has ABS.
slides.fact: With antilock brakes, press firmly and keep steady pressure. The ABS pulses the brakes for you, and pumping can defeat it.

slides.myth: Your tires don't lose pressure just because it got cold.
slides.fact: Tire pressure drops about 1 psi for every 10°F the temperature falls. Check it when the cold hits, using the number on your door jamb sticker.
